perRouteTitles.status: DEFECT FOUND BY THE VERIFIER — FIXED IN CODE IN THIS CORRECTION PASS, then re-proven on the real lineage.
perRouteTitles.whatWasWrong: The shipped build gave EVERY route the identical title `Millwright | AI workflow automation for discrete manufacturing` (all 7 served routes of 2026-08-27T23-36-27-840Z), while the phase reported them as "per-route". The SEO plan's own basis field said so: routes[].title.basis was `content-run:sitePlan.siteIdentity (workingName + category)` — a SITE-level string. Duplicate <title> across every indexable route is a real SEO defect, and NO check in the program measured title uniqueness, which is how it shipped unnoticed.
perRouteTitles.fix: src/seo/production-plan.ts now derives a PER-ROUTE title from the CUSTOMER'S OWN authored content (never the source site, whose titles are forbidden copy). New exported pure function `deriveRouteHeadings(units, slotValues)` reads the content run's own content-units.json (which carries the route each authored unit belongs to) + slot-values.json and applies two rules, in precedence order: (1) `hero-headline` — the route's own hero unit headline slot; (2) `nav-label` — an authored nav/link label whose sibling `.href` slot VALUE is exactly this route key. The title becomes `<heading> | <brand>`; the HOME route deliberately keeps the site-level `<brand> | <category>`, which is the correct homepage title. Nothing is invented, truncated or reworded: a candidate that is empty, head-unsafe, or longer than MAX_ROUTE_HEADING_CHARS (70) is REJECTED and that route keeps the site-level title, with the fallback stated in its own `basis` string. Ties break on sorted slot key, so the derivation is deterministic.
perRouteTitles.detector: New exported `checkTitleUniqueness(plan)` MEASURES duplicate <title>s and names every duplicate group with its routes. It is recorded in the plan-run manifest (checks.titleUniqueness, counts.duplicateTitleRoutes, counts.routeDerivedTitles — all OPTIONAL in the zod schema so plan runs written before this change still load; absence means "not measured", never "zero") and printed by the run (`[seo:plan] titles: 7/8 from the route's own authored heading, 8 distinct across 8 route(s)`). It is deliberately NON-fatal: a duplicate title is a quality defect, and failing the run would delete a title rather than fix one. Independently, isolated-package QA now measures the SERVED bytes: new check `title-uniqueness-measured` (src/production/qa.ts) asserts the measurement ran on every route and that no served title is empty, and carries `duplicate-title-groups=` in its detail — so a plan that PROMISES unique titles and a package that SERVES one repeated string can no longer agree with each other.

perRouteTitles.namedLimitation: A route the content run gave NO authored heading (no hero headline, no nav label pointing at it) still falls back to the site-level title, and if the home route is among the survivors that is a duplicate. On this lineage that case does not occur (7/8 routes heading-derived, home site-level by design, 8/8 distinct), but it is not structurally impossible — which is exactly why the fallback is stated in the route's own `basis`, counted in the manifest, and measured on the served bytes by QA instead of being assumed away. NO SILENT CAP: the 70-character rejection bound and the home-route exemption are both stated here and both visible in the plan's basis strings.
perRouteTitles.safetyOfTheNewTitleSource: The new title source is covered by the SEO plan's EXISTING guards, which is why widening the title's provenance does not widen the leak surface: every planned title/og/twitter string goes through checkForbiddenCopy (byte-equality against every source title/description/og/twitter value) and through checkBrandIsolation, which scans the RENDERED surface (renderedSurfaceOf includes plan titles and the rendered head) against terms derived from the source snapshot — a run whose heading carried the source brand FAILS instead of shipping. Both passed on the real runs (`forbidden-copy PASS (56 comparisons), brand isolation PASS (147 strings vs 3 terms)` on the 8-route build; 49/129 on the 7-route build). A head-unsafe heading cannot reach the head either: candidates are filtered by isHeadSafeText before use and the composed title is still assertHeadSafeText'd.
